meta_title: UK Passport Photo Size (35×45 mm) & Rules for 2026 | Resize-It
meta_description: UK passport photos: 45 × 35 mm printed with a 29–34 mm head, plain cream or light grey background, taken in the last month. Digital: 600 × 750 px minimum. Full rules.
h1: UK Passport Photo Size and Requirements
subtitle: Crop and print 35 × 45 mm photos, checked against the current GOV.UK rules for printed and digital passport photos.

tool_workspace.description: Upload a photo to crop it to the official size. Everything is processed in your browser; nothing is uploaded.

requirements.notes_h3: What to know before you apply

rows.label: Printed size
rows.value: 45 mm high × 35 mm wide, not cut down from a larger picture

rows.label: Head size
rows.value: 29–34 mm from the crown of your head to your chin

rows.label: Background
rows.value: Plain cream or light grey (printed); plain light-coloured (digital)

rows.label: How many
rows.value: 2 identical printed photos for a paper application

rows.label: Printing
rows.value: Professional standard, in colour, on plain white photographic paper with no border

rows.label: Digital photo
rows.value: At least 600 × 750 px and 50 KB–10 MB, in colour, unaltered

rows.label: Glasses
rows.value: Only if you have to. No sunglasses or tinted lenses, and no frames, glare or shadow over your eyes.

rows.label: Expression
rows.value: Plain expression, mouth closed, eyes open and visible, facing forwards

rows.label: Head coverings
rows.value: Only for religious or medical reasons

notes: The photo must have been taken in the last month, which is stricter than most countries.

Applying online with a photo from your own device? GOV.UK asks for your head, shoulders and upper body and says not to crop it, because they crop it for you. Upload the original rather than a cropped version.
Photos with a code from a booth or shop are more likely to be approved than ones taken on your own device.
Printed photos must come out at exactly 45 × 35 mm. Print the PDF sheet at 100% scale, not "fit to page".
Children must be alone in the photo. Under-6s do not need a plain expression, and under-1s do not need their eyes open.
Send printed photos loose, separated from each other and not attached to the form.
requirements.checked: Checked against these sources in November 2026. Rules change, so confirm on the official page before you apply.

how_to.title: How to make a UK passport photo
how_to.step1_text: Stand in front of a plain background in even light and have someone else take the photo at eye level. Follow the UK rules below.
how_to.step2_text: Choose the photo. It is processed in your browser and never uploaded to a server.
how_to.step3_text: Drag the frame to centre your face and use Zoom until your head fills the frame to the size the rules require.
how_to.step4_text: Download the PDF sheet and print it at actual size (100%, no "fit to page") on photo paper, then cut out the photos.

items.q: What size is a UK passport photo?
items.a: Printed photos are 45 mm high and 35 mm wide, and your head must measure 29–34 mm from crown to chin. Digital photos must be at least 600 × 750 px.

items.q: How recent must a UK passport photo be?
items.a: It must have been taken in the last month, for both printed and digital photos.
Printed photos need a plain cream or light grey background. Digital photos need a plain light-coloured background with clear contrast.

items.q: Can I wear glasses in a UK passport photo?
items.a: Only if you have to. They cannot be sunglasses or tinted, and your eyes must not be covered by the frames or by glare, reflection or shadow.

items.q: Should I crop my photo for an online application?
items.a: No. For photos taken on your own device, GOV.UK asks for an uncropped photo showing your head, shoulders and upper body and crops it during the application.
